end.summary:
Practised making one mark for each object to keep track.
Matched marks back to objects to identify missing or extra objects.
Explained a return-check method using one stone for each boat.
Still saw a spread-out row as having more objects than a close row; this was not corrected by the end.
Teach-back was not yet passed.
end.parentNote: Parth practised one-to-one matching by making marks or placing one stone for each object, and successfully used matching to find missing or extra objects. They mixed up spacing with quantity: a spread-out row still has the same number of objects, and this was not corrected later in the lesson. At home, place two rows of the same number of buttons—one spread out and one close—and match each button to check that the quantity stays the same.
